## Answer: 3/8

I did not fully derive this. It rests on my recollection of Czédli's results on congruence counts of finite lattices, so treat it as a well-supported guess rather than a verified result.

**What I can check directly:**
- A chain with $n$ elements has $|\text{Con}| = 2^{n-1}$, so $\text{cd} = 1$. Chains have $|J| = |M| = n-1$, so they are excluded by the hypothesis.
- The 4-element Boolean lattice $2^2$ has $|\text{Con}| = 4$, so $\text{cd} = 1/2$. It has $|J| = |M| = 2$, so it is also excluded.

**What I recall:** For non-chain finite lattices with $n$ elements, $|\text{Con}\,L| \le 2^{n-2}$, which $2^2$ attains. The bound is sharper, $|\text{Con}\,L| \le 3\cdot 2^{n-4}$ (so $\text{cd} \le 3/8$), when $|J(L)| \ne |M(L)|$. Since $2^2$ has equal $J$ and $M$ counts, it does not contradict this sharper bound. I believe the bound is attained, but I did not construct an explicit extremal lattice to confirm it.

ANSWER: 3/8
